about.title: A practical approach to quality
paragraphs: I currently work at DaticsAI, where I test web, mobile, and desktop applications across the development lifecycle. Most days that means writing manual test cases for new features, digging into edge cases nobody thought to mention, and figuring out whether a bug is a one-off or a pattern worth flagging to the whole team.

A good chunk of my work is automation with Playwright, backend validation through Postman, and the occasional JMeter session when a feature needs to prove it can handle real load. I don't automate everything by default. I automate the paths that are stable and worth protecting, and I leave the exploratory, judgment-heavy work to manual testing where it actually belongs.

Before moving into QA I spent time doing front-end development, and that background still shows up in how I work. I can read a component tree, open dev tools and tell you whether a bug is a rendering issue, a state problem, or something coming back wrong from the API. It also means conversations with developers tend to be shorter, because I can usually point at the actual cause instead of just describing the symptom.

expertise.title: Where I focus
expertise.subtitle: Select an area to see how I actually approach it.

areas.label: Functional testing
areas.description: I verify that a feature does what the requirements say, then quietly check the few things the requirements forgot to mention, like what happens on a second attempt or a half-filled form.

areas.label: Regression testing
areas.description: Before a release I re-run the paths that matter most, not the whole app blindly. A change in one module has a habit of breaking something three screens away.

areas.label: Exploratory testing
areas.description: I investigate how real users may behave beyond the documented happy path, including incomplete actions, unexpected navigation, invalid data, and interrupted workflows.

areas.label: UI & usability testing
areas.description: I check whether the interface actually makes sense to use, not just whether it matches the design file. Confusing error states and unclear loading feedback get flagged just as often as visual bugs.

areas.label: API testing
areas.description: I validate requests and responses with Postman, covering expected payloads, missing fields, wrong types, and status codes that don't match what the front end actually expects.

areas.label: Browser automation
areas.description: I build Playwright scripts for the flows that repeat every release, login, checkout-style journeys, form submissions, so the team gets fast feedback without re-testing the same thing by hand each time.

areas.label: Performance & load testing
areas.description: In approved QA environments I use JMeter to see how an endpoint behaves under concurrent requests, where response times start to drift, and where the system actually breaks.

areas.label: Cross-browser & compatibility testing
areas.description: I check layout, behavior, and timing-sensitive interactions across browsers and screen sizes, since the bug that never shows up on your machine is usually waiting on someone else's.

areas.label: Defect reporting & verification
areas.description: I write defect reports a developer can act on immediately: exact steps, expected versus actual behavior, environment, and evidence. Then I verify the fix against the original scenario, not just a quick glance.

areas.label: Requirements & user-flow analysis
areas.description: I map out the user flow before writing test cases so I know which paths are critical, which are edge cases, and where the requirements are actually ambiguous.

automation.title: How a test goes from idea to regression coverage
automation.subtitle: A short walk through the pipeline I use to turn a requirement into something the whole team can rely on.

cards.title: Playwright automation
cards.description: End-to-end scripts for login, navigation, and critical workflows, written to fail with a clear reason instead of a vague timeout.

cards.title: API validation with Postman
cards.description: Collections that check status codes, response shape, and failure handling before the front end ever touches the endpoint.

cards.title: JMeter performance testing
cards.description: Load profiles run in approved QA environments to see how response times hold up as concurrent users increase.

cards.title: Regression suite design
cards.description: A curated set of checks that protect the paths that matter, kept lean on purpose so failures are meaningful, not noise.

cards.title: Reusable test data and structure
cards.description: Fixtures and page objects shared across scripts, so a UI change means updating one file, not fifteen.

cards.title: Failure evidence and reporting
cards.description: Screenshots, traces, and step logs attached to every failing run, so a developer can see exactly what happened without reproducing it first.

systems.title: Complex workflows across products
systems.subtitle: Select a node to see common risks and how I test it.

nodes.label: Authentication
nodes.risks: Session handling, token expiry, and inconsistent behavior across tabs or logout flows.
nodes.approach: I check login, logout, session expiry, and concurrent sessions across devices, including what happens when a token goes stale mid-action.

nodes.label: Payments
nodes.risks: Failed or partial transactions, duplicate charges, and unclear states when a payment is interrupted.
nodes.approach: I test successful and failed payment paths, interrupted transactions, and how the UI communicates a pending or failed state to the user.

nodes.label: KYC verification
nodes.risks: Ambiguous rejection reasons and inconsistent handling of edge-case documents.
nodes.approach: I focus on negative scenarios: invalid documents, mismatched data, and whether rejection messaging actually helps the user correct the problem.

nodes.label: Role-based access
nodes.risks: Permission boundaries that leak between roles, especially after a role change.
nodes.approach: I verify each role sees and can do only what it should, and I specifically test behavior right after a permission change.

nodes.label: Cloud file imports
nodes.risks: Large files, unsupported formats, and interrupted uploads leaving the system in a half-finished state.
nodes.approach: I test normal imports alongside oversized files, wrong formats, and connection drops mid-upload to see how gracefully the system recovers.

nodes.label: Real-time chat
nodes.risks: Message ordering, delivery gaps, and state drift between connected clients.
nodes.approach: I test message delivery across multiple clients, reconnect scenarios, and ordering when messages arrive close together.

nodes.label: AI-generated content
nodes.risks: Inconsistent output quality, unclear loading states, and failure handling when generation doesn't complete.
nodes.approach: I treat generation as a multi-state process, testing the loading, partial, and failure states as carefully as the final output.

nodes.label: Data validation
nodes.risks: Invalid input silently accepted, or valid input incorrectly rejected.
nodes.approach: I test boundary values, wrong types, and malformed input against both the UI and the API directly to confirm validation matches on both sides.

nodes.label: Error recovery
nodes.risks: Errors that leave the app in a stuck or inconsistent state instead of recovering cleanly.
nodes.approach: I deliberately trigger failures mid-flow to see whether the app recovers, retries, or just gets stuck with no way forward.

nodes.label: Cross-platform behavior
nodes.risks: Features that behave differently across web, mobile, and desktop builds of the same product.
nodes.approach: I compare the same workflow across platforms, looking for timing differences, layout issues, and behavior that only breaks on one build.

principles.title: Understand the user journey before writing test cases
principles.description: I'd rather spend twenty minutes mapping out how someone actually moves through a feature than write ten test cases for the wrong path.

principles.title: Test beyond the happy path
principles.description: The happy path almost always works. I'm more interested in what happens when someone double-clicks submit, goes back mid-flow, or enters something nobody expected.

principles.title: Make every defect easy to reproduce
principles.description: A bug report a developer can't reproduce is just a conversation starter, not a fix. I write steps, evidence, and expected-versus-actual so the issue speaks for itself.

principles.title: Automate stable, valuable regression paths, not everything blindly
principles.description: Automation is a tool, not a goal. I automate the flows that are stable and worth protecting, and I keep exploring the rest by hand where judgment actually matters.
